A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AGUVIS research. Their text, figures, tables, mathematical formulation, and Appendices A–E support comparison. The empty appendix contents page in v2 is a navigation defect, not missing scientific material.

before.justification: v1 reports original AGUVIS benchmark results, training ablations, error analyses, and a 90-sample human assessment of augmented data.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses and reports revised scores and additional OSWorld configurations.

M1.justification: The specified inner monologue changes from Observation, Thought, and Low-level Instruction to just Thought and Low-level Instruction. This removal appears in Sections 2.2–2.3 and the Stage-2 training schema in Appendix C.1. Backbones, action space, grounding packing, and two-stage training remain unchanged; retraining is not established.

E1.justification: Training sources and coverage in Tables 10–11 are unchanged, as are the web, mobile, desktop, grounding, and planning benchmarks. OSWorld already appears in v1 Table 6. The human study, error-analysis samples, and qualitative scenarios also existed in v1.

E2.justification: The OSWorld comparison adds Claude Computer-Use and OpenAI Operator in v2 Table 8. Multimodal-Mind2Web Table 2 removes the standalone CogAgent comparator. SeeClick remains, now labeled SeeClick-9.6B with revised result reporting; its size label alone does not establish a new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds an OSWorld configuration pairing GPT-4o with AGUVIS-72B as grounder; v1 paired GPT-4o only with AGUVIS-7B. The established evaluation metrics, AndroidControl's 500 sampled step-actions, training budgets, and appendix evaluation procedures otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The main training-stage and inner-monologue ablation revises its full-model reference scores, changing the reported ablation contrasts. The backbone, data-mixture, packing, enforced-planning, human-quality, and case analyses otherwise remain. The cross-platform ablation highlighted in v2 Table 7 already appeared in v1 Appendix E.1.2.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark comparisons. The human-study and error-analysis sample counts and reporting practices are retained.

E6.justification: OSWorld's reported GPT-4o/AGUVIS-7B score changes from 11.07 to 14.79, and GPT-4o/AGUVIS-72B is newly reported at 17.04. Table 2 replaces and expands SeeClick scores and removes CogAgent results. The main ablation's Mind2Web reference changes from 58.5/55.4/54.8 to 60.4/54.6/56.6, while appendix Tables 14 and 17 retain the earlier values. Most other scores are unchanged; these revisions do not establish controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation and its transition and observation functions are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. The inner-monologue revision changes the procedural output schema rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified pure-vision GUI framework, standardized actions, augmented grounding/reasoning data, two-stage training, and autonomous inference without external closed-source planners. The principal performance, efficiency, and cross-platform contribution claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 newly identifies inability to express uncertainty or refuse ambiguous actions and difficulty recognizing semantically complex instructions. It proposes refusal-oriented training, complexity annotations, and adaptive planning thresholds. v2 also expands the desktop-transfer interpretation and explicitly leaves open-source replacement of GPT-4o data augmentation to future work.

D1.justification: v1 promises future release; v2 states that datasets, models, and training recipes have been released through the same project site. This is a reported availability change, not independently verified access. Appendix C.2 retains the hardware, hyperparameters, and training times, while v1's explicit online viewport-resolution statement is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of OS-ATLAS, mobile planning/reflection approaches, and newer VLM references including Molmo and Qwen2.5-VL. It removes the Agent-FLAN/AgentTuning comparison and WonderBread discussion. These update the surrounding literature without substantially redefining AGUVIS's central positioning.

P1.justification: Most main-text sections are extensively rewritten. The contribution bullets become narrative prose, the analysis is reorganized around training stages, inner monologue, and cross-platform benefits, and an Impact Statement is added. Dataset terminology and numerous explanations and cross-references are revised.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout, replaces the training-overview figure with an interaction diagram, and adds a data-augmentation diagram. Tables are reorganized, existing appendix ablations are redisplayed in the main text, and prompt boxes are restyled. The appendix contents entries disappear, leaving only their heading.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition through the framework and augmentation diagrams, better-integrated analysis, broader OSWorld comparisons, and more explicit deployment limitations. These are useful but limited gains because most empirical evidence already existed. Experimental traceability remains problematic: Appendix D.2 no longer matches Table 2, ablation scores remain inconsistent across the main text and appendices, and the output-schema revision is not connected to experimental reruns.
